name: Register.Domains Domain Check
author: registerdomains

sections.description:
Domain Check adds a block and a shortcode that answer, inside your site, the questions people have about a domain name:

  • Is it available? The answer shows when it was checked, and it never says “Taken” unless that is confirmed.
  • What does it cost? First-year and renewal list prices in USD, side by side, and the minimum registration period.
  • What does the registry ask for? Local presence, documents, and whether a Trustee (local contact) service exists and its price. What has not been verified says “Not verified”.
  • If it is taken, who has it? On request: registrar, dates, statuses, name servers and DNSSEC. Never registrant contacts.

Links to Register.Domains are off by default. Without them the block is purely informative.

Searches run only when a visitor presses the button. Nothing is searched when a page loads or while typing.

The plugin gets its site key from Register.Domains when you connect it: there is nothing to request or wait for. A site can use the service without being an affiliate.

External services

This is the official plugin of Register.Domains (https://register.domains), a domain registrar, and it is published by Register.Domains LLC. It relies on one external service: the Register.Domains REST API at https://rest.register.domains, operated by Register.Domains LLC. The plugin uses it to look up domain names and to obtain list prices and registration requirements. It sends nothing until the site administrator ticks “Connect to Register.Domains” and saves the settings.

What is sent, and when

  • When the administrator saves with “Connect to Register.Domains” ticked and the site has no key yet: the address of the site (its Site Address, as in Settings > General) and the version of the plugin. Register.Domains answers with a key for this site and a site id. It keeps the address, the version, the date and a hash of the key; not the key itself. The request comes from the server of your site, and Register.Domains uses its IP address, in memory only, to limit how many keys and searches one server gets.
  • When the administrator ticks “Disconnect” and saves: the site key, so that Register.Domains disables it. The key is removed from your site even if that request fails.
  • When a visitor submits the form: the domain name, with the site key that identifies your site.
  • When a visitor presses “See registry details”: the domain name, with the site key.
  • When the search limit of the site is spent: the extension of the name, to keep showing its prices. The site key goes with it.
  • When the administrator presses “Test connection”: a request for the price of .com, with the site key.

Visitor IP addresses, cookies, page addresses and the affiliate code are not sent. The browser of the visitor talks only to your site, and your site calls the service.

Why

To look up the name in the registries and to answer with the list prices and requirements of Register.Domains. To answer, the name reaches the availability and registry sources that Register.Domains queries.

Retention

Register.Domains keeps checked names in a short cache: 10 minutes for available names and for registry details, one hour for taken names. Its usage logs do not contain the names.

On your site, names and their results are cached for 3 minutes and extension data for 6 hours. For the limit per visitor, the site keeps a keyed hash of the IP address for one hour. The plugin never stores the IP address in clear. WordPress deletes expired entries in its daily cleanup.

Terms

  • Privacy Policy: https://register.domains/en/terms/privacy-policy
  • Terms and Conditions: https://register.domains/en/terms/terms-and-conditions

Affiliate links

The affiliate code is optional and empty by default. If the administrator turns on the links and enters a code issued by Register.Domains, ?ref=<code> is added to the links to a domain name and to an extension page on register.domains. It is not added to privacy, terms or support links, it is not sent to the API and it is not logged. These links carry rel="sponsored".

With a code, the block always shows this notice to visitors: “This site may earn a commission from Register.Domains when you register a domain through these links.” It cannot be turned off. The plugin loads no tracking script.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin and activate it. Activating it contacts nobody.
  2. In Settings > Domain Check, read what is sent, tick “Connect to Register.Domains” and save. The site gets its key at that moment. If Register.Domains gave you a key, paste it under “I already have a key” instead.
  3. Press “Test connection”.
  4. Add the “Domain Check” block to a page, or use the shortcode [regdom_domain_check]. It accepts heading and placeholder.
sections.faq:
Does it register domains or take payments?

No.

Why does a search say “Could not confirm”?

The source could not tell whether the name is registered or the lookup failed. The plugin does not guess.

Why did a search stop working for a while?

Each visitor has 10 searches per hour on your site, and each site has limits on the service. The message says when to try again.

My site is behind a proxy and all visitors share the limit

The plugin only trusts REMOTE_ADDR, because forwarded headers can be forged. If your proxy is trustworthy, return the real address from the regdom_visitor_ip filter.

Why are international names refused?

Converting them needs the PHP intl extension. Ask your host to turn it on.
sections.changelog:
0.3.0

  • New name and slug: Register.Domains Domain Check (register-domains-domain-check).
  • One prefix, regdom, for classes, constants, options, transients, the shortcode (now [regdom_domain_check]), the block and the REST routes.
  • The readme names the API endpoint, rest.register.domains, under External services.

0.2.1

  • Text domain is now register-domains-domain-check, the slug of the plugin on WordPress.org.
  • The header no longer has a Plugin URI equal to the Author URI.

0.2.0

  • Connecting gets the site key from Register.Domains at once. A key you were given can still be pasted.
  • Disconnect: removes the key from the site and asks Register.Domains to disable it.

0.1.1

  • Default API address rest.register.domains.
  • Form controls use the font of the theme.
  • A taken name no longer shows registration prices.

0.1.0

  • First pilot version.
